groups.reason: ConfirmActionDialog is a destructive-action confirmation with its own cancel-first focus and explicit affirmative step; SubjectWindow is a read-only subject panel using a GameWindow shell. Their only shared call in this lexical gate is the keyboard claim, not duplicated decision authority.

The same Map.get/set lexical signature masks different behavior. Genealogy has one shared findFamilyGroupRoot path-compression implementation used by familyTree and genealogyRegistry for temporary family-group maps; simDelta.relationshipFieldCoverage instead tracks which relationship payload revisions were sent to the worker replica. Different data ownership and contracts; no remaining duplicate union-find implementation.

resolveSessionSpeaker resolves a specific dialogue participant by identity and returns that participant or null. humanSocial.byId is a numerical sort comparator that orders neighboring settlers by id. The gate sees only the shared id property read, not a common decision or implementation.

relationships.pushToGroup builds sampled Entity groups used by the relationship simulation, whereas workforce.pushId builds numeric occupant-ID arrays for staffing snapshots. Their small Map append idiom is the same but their domain-owned data, element types, and ordering contracts differ; coupling the owners would introduce a cross-subsystem dependency for a trivial operation.

pathfinding.lineCrossesBlocked's local isBlocked checks each traversed grid cell for obstruction and cliff elevation differences; stripBuild.inferStripRotation uses the absolute drag delta to choose a horizontal (0 degree) or vertical (90 degree) segment. Both happen to call Math.abs, the only shared lexical feature. They have separate inputs, outputs, owners, and no common behavior to refactor; coupling them would corrupt navigation or strip geometry.
